(d) The five-year accident history;
In the past five years, no accidental releases from covered processes that result in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on site, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage had occurred. 

(e) The emergency response program; 
MAYS developed an Emergency Response Plan to establish policies, procedures, and an organizational structure for a coordinated response to emergencies, particularly accidental regulated substances released to protect facility personnel, public health and the environment. The plan includes the following sections.
1.	Facility information, including relevant information about the facility and surrounding characteristics, regulated substance information, a worst case and alternative case accidental release information. 
2.	Internal notification procedure to be executed by any employee that discovers and emergency. 
3.	External Notification procedure to be activated by the Emergency Coordinator in order to informing the public and the appropriate Federal, State, and local emergency response agencies about accidental releases.
4.	Evacuation Plan to be implemented by all employees after the internal alarm system is activated, including evacuation maps, meeting point count, among others. 
5.	Emergency Operation Plan, including initial activities to be executed by the emergency response team, specific response strategies to be implemented in case of an accidental release of any regulated substance store or use in the facility over the threshold, 
6.	Recovery plan to be implemented once the emergency response is completed and the accidental release is controlled.  
7.	Training requirements for emergency response team personnel and for all employees.

General Facility Information
Mays Chemical Company of Puerto Rico, Inc. (dba MAYS Ochoa) is a company engaged in the chemical distributor industry located in Catano, Puerto Rico. The main activity carried out at the facility (stationary sources) is the receiving, storage and distribution of chemical substances and related materials. Materials are stored in either closed warehouses or outdoor areas in designated areas across the facility. The facility receives materials included in this RMP already in their end use package. The worst-case scenario is the possibility of a container rupture during handling or storage operations. The most credible scenario is the possibility of a container opening and regulated substances controlled release, due to a safety devices activation).  

In addition, a new process is included in this RMP revision to start up a Sodium Hypochlorite manufacturing operation in a dedicated building at the facility. The new process includes storage, handling and use of liquid chlorine as a raw material for sodium hypochlorite manufacturing operations. 

The worst-case scenario is the possibility of the release of one (1) containers rupture during handling or storage operations.  The most credible scenario is the possibility of chlorine release during container connection or disconnection or a hose failure. 

(a) The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source;
MAYS is committed to protecting the health, safety and welfare of the nearest community and also the environment as part of its operations. For this reason, MAYS has developed the Emergency Response Plan to strive to minimize the impact of emergencies and maximize the effectiveness of the facility emergency response teams response to, and recover from, the incident. 
The Emergency Response Plan is designed to help MAYS employees, under the leadership of the Emergency Response Coordinator, to respond appropriately when emergency conditions exist. Thi

s plan allows for an immediate and coordinated response by MAYS Emergency Response Committee, thereby minimizing danger to our facility, employees, nearest community and the environment.

(b) The stationary source and regulated substances handled;
The regulated substances handled in the covered processes are 1) Ammonia Anhydrous, 2) Chlorine and 3) Ethylene Oxide 
Ammonia Anhydrous is received in ISO-Tank and stored outdoors in a designated area away from normal traffic. ISO-Tank valves are not manipulated in the facility. 
Chlorine is received in freight containers. Containers are handled with a dedicated forklift with a lifting device. Containers are stored in a roofed designated area away from incompatible materials. Containers are provided with a cover to protect valves. Containers valves are not manipulated at the facility. 
Ethyle Oxide is received in freight containers. Drums are handled with a dedicated electrically classified forklift. Drums are stored in a dedicated non-combustible and electrically classified building. Drums valves are not manipulated at the facility. 
Chlorine is also received for a manufacturing process (a separate covered process) that is conducted in the facility. Chlorine containers are handled using a dedicated forklift with a lifting device. Chlorine containers are stored inside the manufacturing building. Containers are transferred using a dedicated crane. Chlorine containers are connected to a chlorine manifold to add Chlorine to a mixer tank. 

(c) The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps;
General accidental release prevention program 
1.	Facility is fully fenced and monitored by Security Surveillance Camera 24/7. 
2.	An Emergency Response team is available in the facility. 
3.	Emergency response equipment and materials are available in the facility, including Level A suits, SCBA, among others. 
4.	Emergency equipment and materials are periodically inspected. 
5.	Portable Fire extin

guisher and three (3) Wheeled Extinguisher are located in strategic locations. 
6.	Spill kits are located in strategic locations.
7.	Personnel receive training in multiple topics associated with precautions and release prevention.
8.	The facility is provided with mechanism to contain stormwater in case that an emergency cause any type of pollution.  
9.	Equipment are included in a mechanical integrity program.
10.	Operating procedures are in placed to be followed by personnel at all times. 
Ammonia Storage specific prevention steps
1.	ISO-Tank storage area is located in a dedicated area with low vehicle traffic. 
2.	Area is inspected on a weekly basis. 
3.	ISO-Tanks are inspected every 2.5 years and 5.0 years. 
4.	Containers do not exceed 29,000 pounds. 
5.	ISO-Tank valves are not manipulated on the site. 
6.	A water hose is located near the area to be used for water spray response strategy during an emergency. 
Chlorine Storage specific prevention steps
1.	Containers are stored in a roofed area. 
2.	Area is inspected on a weekly basis. 
3.	A temperature transmitter is located in the area and triggers a notification in case temperature exceeds the set point. 
4.	A Kit B is available at the facility to response to any release. Kit B is periodically inspected. 
5.	A dedicated forklift, with a lifting device, is used to handle Chlorine Containers.
6.	Containers are provided with a cover to protect valves. 
7.	Containers valves are not manipulated on the site. 
8.	Containers are stored in a maximum of two (2) level piles. 
9.	Chlorine containers are stored aways of incompatible materials. 
Ethylene Oxide Storage specific prevention steps
1.	Building access is limited. 
2.	Building is constructed with non-combustible materials. 
3.	Building is dedicated only for Ethylene Oxide Drums storage. 
4.	Area is electrically classified. 
5.	Area is inspected on a weekly basis. 
6.	Four (4) electrically classified exhaust fans are installed in the building to provide mechanical ve

ntilation that exceeds the Puerto Rico Building Code requirements. 
7.	A temperature transmitter is located in the area and triggers a notification in case temperature exceeds the set point. 
8.	A dedicated electrically classified Forklift is used to handle Drums. 
9.	Containers valves are not manipulated in the site. 
Chlorine Use at Manufacturing Process specific prevention steps
1.	Access to the building is limited. 
2.	All operations are conducted indoors. 
3.	Area is inspected on a weekly basis. 
4.	Containers are stored over trunnions.
5.	A Dedicated Crane is used to transfer Chlorine Containers from the Storage Area to the Manufacturing Bench. 
6.	The Bench is provided with trunnions.  
7.	The Manufacturing process is controlled by Plant PLC with prompts to be completed by the operator.
8.	Operating procedure is in place for operators. 
9.	The Batch Plant is provided with multiples interlocks that close the chlorine pneumatic valves in case of any deviation of normal operations. 
10.	The Batch Plant is provided with an emergency stop that stops the process and closes all valves.
11.	Chlorine sensors are located next to chlorine areas with interlock to closed chlorine pneumatic valves (in the manifold and in each container)
12.	Chlorine Manifold is provided with a barometric loop, three (3) rupture disks and expansion tank
13.	Chlorine manifold is provided with three pneumatic valves and each cylinder is provided with a pneumatic valve connected directly to the container liquid valve. 
14.	Chlorine pneumatic valves are failure to closed. 
15.	Leak tests are conducted by operators during chlorine container connection operations. 
16.	Pressure tests at the Chlorine manifold are conducted before chlorine addition. 
17.	Chlorine Manifold is maintained empty, except when chlorine is added to the mixer tank. 
18.	Chlorine manifold is padded with air after chlorine addition is completed.

The emergency response plan also includes a Contact list for internal personnel and external emergency response agencies and resources, documentation of proper first-aid and emergency medical treatment necessary to treat accidental human exposures and procedures and measures for emergency response after an accidental release of each regulated substance store and use in the facility over the regulatory threshold. 

(f) Planned changes to improve safety.
No changes to improve safety is in progress to be implemented. However, employee training, emergency drills, covered process evaluation, among other initiatives are planned to be executed to confirm the safety in the covered process and to identify opportunity areas and to establish corrective actions for continues improvement of covered processes safety.
